Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

I just checked, and it looks like there’s no signal showing at the top of my phone, and it says data is disabled. I’m not sure what that means—does that mean I can’t make calls or use the internet either? What should I do next?

I followed your steps and gave the messaging app permission for both storage and SMS, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to worry this might never work.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called? It’s been a few hours now and they just won’t go through. I’m not very good with all this tech stuff, so I’d really appreciate some help getting it working again.

Thank you for reaching out about your MMS (picture message) issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (for verification)?

Once I have this information, I’ll guide you step-by-step to resolve the MMS issue.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

Thank you, John. I’ve found your account. To help you send picture messages (MMS) again, I’ll walk you through a few steps to diagnose and fix the issue.

First, could you please check if you can make regular calls and if your mobile data (internet) is working for other apps, like browsing the web? This will help us determine if the problem is with your overall service or just MMS.

Let me know if you can make calls and use mobile data, or if you’re having trouble with those as well.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

I just checked, and it looks like there’s no signal showing at the top of my phone, and it says data is disabled. I’m not sure what that means—does that mean I can’t make calls or use the internet either? What should I do next?

Thank you for checking. If there’s no signal and data is disabled, that means your phone currently can’t make calls, use the internet, or send MMS. Let’s try to get your basic service working first.

Please check if Airplane Mode is turned on by looking for an airplane icon at the top of your screen. If you see it, please turn Airplane Mode off.

After you check Airplane Mode, let me know if the signal returns or if you still see “no signal.” If you’re not sure how to check, let me know and I’ll guide you through the steps.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I checked again, and I don’t see any airplane icon at the top of my screen—just the “no signal” and “data disabled” messages. What should I try next?

Thank you for confirming. The next step is to check your SIM card, as issues with the SIM can cause loss of signal and data.

Please try the following:
1. Power off your phone.
2. Remove the SIM card from its slot.
3. Wait a few seconds, then reinsert the SIM card securely.
4. Power your phone back on.

After your phone restarts, check if you now have a signal or if the “no signal” and “data disabled” messages are still there. Let me know what you see after doing this.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Alright, I followed your instructions and now I see bars for signal, it says “5G,” and data is enabled at the top of my screen. Does that mean it’s working now? What should I do next?

That’s great news! Seeing signal bars, “5G,” and data enabled means your phone is now connected to the network and mobile data is working. 

Let’s check if you can send picture messages (MMS) now. Please try sending a picture message to someone. If it goes through, your issue is resolved.

If you still can’t send MMS, let me know what happens (any error messages or if it just doesn’t send), and I’ll guide you through the next steps.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I tried to send a picture message just now, but it still won’t go through. There’s no specific error message—it just doesn’t send. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your signal and data are working but MMS still won’t send, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for MMS to work.

Could you please check your APN settings on your phone and let me know if you see anything unusual, or if you’re not sure how to check, I can guide you through the process or provide steps to reset them to default. Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and there’s something called an MMSC URL listed too. I’m not sure if that’s right or not—should I reset these settings, or is there something else I should do?

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Since there is an APN name and an MMSC URL listed, the settings might be correct, but sometimes resetting them can resolve hidden issues.

Let’s try resetting your APN settings to default. After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your device?

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve reset the APN settings as you suggested. Do I need to restart my phone now? I always get a bit nervous about restarting—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do this?

You will not lose any of your photos, messages, or personal data by restarting your phone. Restarting simply refreshes your phone’s system and applies the new APN settings.

Please go ahead and restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try sending a picture message (MMS) again and let me know if it works.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t this working? Is there anything else we can try?

Thank you for your patience. Since you’ve reset your APN settings, restarted your phone, and still can’t send MMS, let’s check a few more things that can affect MMS:

1. Is your phone currently connected to Wi-Fi, and is Wi-Fi Calling enabled?
2. Are you able to send and receive regular text messages (SMS)?
3. Do you know if your messaging app has permission to access storage and SMS?

Please let me know about your Wi-Fi connection and Wi-Fi Calling status first. If you’re not sure how to check, I can guide you through it.
Wi-Fi is turned OFF.

Thank you for confirming that Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi Calling are both off. Next, let’s check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS, specifically access to storage and SMS.

Could you check your messaging app’s permissions and make sure it has permission to access both storage and SMS? If you’re not sure how to do this, let me know your phone type (Android or iPhone), and I can provide step-by-step instructions.

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for the phone. It doesn’t mention storage or SMS. Should I change something here? I’m not sure how to do that.

Yes, your messaging app needs permission to access both storage and SMS to send and receive picture messages (MMS).

Could you please let me know if you’re using an Android phone or an iPhone? I’ll provide you with simple, step-by-step instructions to grant the necessary permissions for your messaging app.
I’m using an Android phone. Could you please walk me through how to give the messaging app those permissions? I get a bit lost with these settings.

Absolutely! Here’s how you can grant storage and SMS permissions to your messaging app on an Android phone:

1. Open the Settings app on your phone.
2. Scroll down and tap Apps (or Apps & notifications).
3. Find and tap on your Messaging app (it might be called “Messages” or something similar).
4. Tap Permissions.
5. Look for Storage and SMS in the list:
   - If you see Storage or SMS under “Denied,” tap on each one and select Allow.
6. Once both permissions are allowed, exit Settings.

After you’ve done this, try sending a picture message (MMS) again. Let me know if it works or if you need any more help!

Since you have signal, data, correct APN settings, Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi Calling are off, and the messaging app has the right permissions, we’ve covered all the standard troubleshooting steps for MMS issues.
